understanding: Temporary quick-testing contract for uart_config: program LCR format, DLAB-gated divisor MSB-first LSB-next, FIFO trigger and IER in dependency order via wishbone_bus after clock and reset bring-up, with directed corners then symbolic sweep; all QUICK_TEST_PLAN_APPROVAL details remain INFERRED, not engineer approval.
preconditions: Clock is stable at selected period and reset bring-up from t_bringup_clk is complete with idle cycles observed
wishbone_bus base read write and DLAB-gated divisor sequences from t_wb_seq are available via explicit wishbone_bus sequencer handle
DUT is in DATA_BUS_WIDTH_8 build with 3-bit wb_adr_i and 8-bit data; uart_config virtual sequence runs on virtual sequencer with no VIFs or delays
QUICK_TEST_PLAN_APPROVAL intentions are INFERRED temporary test-only approvals, not engineer sign-off; only quoted source text constrains behavior
stimulus_steps: WAIT for t_bringup_clk completion THEN OBTAIN explicit handle to wishbone_bus sequencer; START uart_config on null virtual sequencer with sequencer-handle switch and no VIFs or delays with timing tracked to selected clock period

FOR directed bring-up corners via wishbone_bus sequencer only in dependency order per f_dlab_set_1 to f_ier_step_5: WRITE LCR at 3 with DLAB 1 THEN WRITE divisor MSB at 1 first THEN LSB at 0 THEN WRITE LCR at 3 with DLAB 0 THEN WRITE FCR at 2 with trigger THEN WRITE IER at 1; INCLUDE reset-all-disabled with IER 0, max-trigger 11, and DLAB-set-blocking-normal-0to1 case

FOR sweep over SYM_LCR_CHAR SYM_STOP SYM_PARITY SYM_DIV_MSB SYM_DIV_LSB SYM_TRIG SYM_IER under set-then-clear DLAB constraint: SPAWN wishbone_bus write and read children per iteration; per-agent sequences drive only wishbone_bus interface
IF serial_data or modem_control_if traffic is required THEN SPAWN only their own agents separately; uart_config virtual sequence itself drives nothing directly
check_steps: COMPARE DLAB gating per f_dlab_block_6 and f_dlab_gate_7: IF DLAB is 1 THEN only divisor LSB at addr 0 and MSB at addr 1 are routed AND normal RB_THR at 0 and IER at 1 are blocked; IF DLAB is 0 THEN reverse
COMPARE LCR readback per f_lcr_read_22: WAIT wishbone_bus read at addr 3 THEN COMPARE observed data equals programmed format for sampled LCR values

COMPARE divisor and IER persistence: WAIT wishbone_bus read of divisor LSB_MSB with DLAB 1 and IER with DLAB 0 THEN COMPARE observed data equals last programmed SYM_DIV and SYM_IER excluding FCR which is write-only
coverage_steps: SAMPLE cg_divisor per f_divlsb_addr_11 and f_divmsb_addr_12 via dedicated subscriber tapping wishbone_bus monitor analysis port on divisor write with DLAB set: bins zero max mid_low mid_high

SAMPLE dlab_addr_map and wb_addr_x_dlab per f_dlab_block_6 and f_dlab_gate_7 via dedicated subscriber tapping wishbone_bus monitor on ACK with DLAB state: normal_0_DLAB0 normal_1_DLAB0 divlsb_0_DLAB1 divmsb_1_DLAB1 other_2to6

SAMPLE LCR format per f_lcr_char_13, FCR trigger per f_fcr_trigvals_17 and IER enables per f_ier_bits_18 via dedicated subscriber tapping wishbone_bus monitor analysis port; drivers never supply coverage
completion: WAIT all spawned wishbone_bus children complete OR UNTIL TESTBENCH request_timeout_cycles expires as operational limit only
DRAIN wishbone_bus monitor for drain_cycles as TESTBENCH operational limit then close uart_config virtual sequence
CLEANUP deassert wb_stb_i and wb_cyc_i via wishbone_bus driver, return wishbone_bus to idle, release explicit sequencer handles, leave serial_data and modem_control_if untouched

facts.statement: Initialization requires LCR bit 7 set to 1 before divisor access.
facts.quote:
Set bit 7 to ‘1’
to allow access to the Divisor Latches.

facts.statement: Divisor must be programmed MSB first then LSB next.
facts.quote: Set the Divisor Latches, MSB first, LSB next.

facts.statement: After divisor, LCR bit 7 must be cleared to 0 for normal registers.
facts.quote: Set bit 7 of LCR to ‘0’ to disable access to Divisor Latches.

facts.statement: FIFO trigger is programmed after LCR and divisor setup.
facts.quote: Set the FIFO trigger level.

facts.statement: IER enables are programmed after FIFO trigger.
facts.quote:
Enable desired interrupts by setting appropriate bits in the Interrupt Enable
register.

facts.statement: When DLAB is 1 normal registers at addresses 0-1 cannot be accessed.
facts.quote: At this time the above registers at addresses 0-1 can’t be accessed.

facts.statement: Divisor registers are accessible only when LCR DLAB bit is 1.
facts.quote:
The registers can be accessed when the 7th (DLAB) bit of the Line Control Register is set
to ‘1’.

facts.statement: LCR is at bus address 3 with 8-bit RW access.
facts.quote: Line Control Register 3 8 RW Control connection

facts.statement: FCR is at bus address 2 with write-only control.
facts.quote: FIFO Control 2 8 W Control FIFO options

facts.statement: IER is at bus address 1 with 8-bit RW access.
facts.quote: Interrupt Enable 1 8 RW Enable/Mask interrupts

facts.statement: Divisor LSB is at address 0 with 8-bit RW access.
facts.quote: Divisor Latch Byte 1 (LSB) 0 8 RW The LSB of the divisor

facts.statement: Divisor MSB is at address 1 with 8-bit RW access.
facts.quote: Divisor Latch Byte 2 1 8 RW The MSB of the divisor

facts.statement: LCR bits 1-0 select character length.
facts.quote: 1-0 RW Select number of bits in each character

facts.statement: LCR bit 7 is DLAB access control.
facts.quote: 7 RW Divisor Latch Access bit.

facts.statement: DLAB 1 selects divisor latches and 0 selects normal registers.
facts.quote:
‘1’ – The divisor latches can be accessed
 ‘0’ – The normal registers are accessed

facts.statement: FCR bits 7-6 define receiver FIFO trigger level.
facts.quote: 7-6 W Define the Receiver FIFO Interrupt trigger level

facts.statement: FCR trigger 00 selects 1 byte, 01 selects 4, 10 selects 8, 11 selects 14.
facts.quote:
‘00’ – 1 byte
 ‘01’ – 4 bytes
 ‘10’ – 8 bytes
 ‘11’ – 14 bytes

facts.statement: IER bit 0 enables RX-data and bit 1 enables THR-empty.
facts.quote:
0 RW Received Data available interrupt
 ‘0’ – disabled
 ‘1’ – enabled
1 RW Transmitter Holding Register empty interrupt

facts.statement: IER bit 2 enables receiver line status interrupt.
facts.quote: 2 RW Receiver Line Status Interrupt

facts.statement: IER bit 3 enables modem status interrupt.
facts.quote: 3 RW Modem Status Interrupt

facts.statement: IER bits 7-4 are reserved and must be logic 0.
facts.quote: 7-4 RW Reserved. Should be logic ‘0’.

facts.statement: LCR may be read to check current line settings.
facts.quote:
Reading from the register is allowed to check the current
settings of the communication.

questions: Confirm legal LCR, divisor, trigger and IER values and programming order including character-length stop parity stick break combinations, divisor zero legality, and MSB-first LSB-next with set-then-clear DLAB?

Are write and read addresses literal 3-bit wb_adr_i pin values 0 to 6 with LCR at 3 FCR at 2 IER at 1 divisor LSB at 0 MSB at 1, what is legality of addr 7, and does DLAB 1 route 0 to LSB and 1 to MSB while blocking normal 0 to 1?

What is active level of wb_rst_i and inactive levels of wb_stb_i wb_cyc_i wb_we_i, what is legal wb_sel_i with 4-bit sel and 8-bit data, and what are request_timeout_cycles drain_cycles and WB_ACK_O latency plus back-to-back idle rule for config accesses?
What are constrained-random legal masks and comparison masks for LCR IER FCR divisor given DLAB-banked fields, and how are reserved IER 7-4 and write-only FCR handled in mirrors and scoreboards?
How must serial_data data_bits parity stop_bits and bit_cycles track the LCR sweep, and must configuration bus writes agree with serial driver and monitor settings?

What are owners or tie_offs for all DUT inputs during uart_config: wishbone_bus drives WB inputs, but what drives srx_pad_i cts_pad_i dsr_pad_i ri_pad_i dcd_pad_i and observes stx_pad_o rts_pad_o dtr_pad_o int_o?
How do sweep_level knob, seeds, uniform exhaustive versus corner-biased reset-all-disabled and max-trigger cases, and predictor update for configured divisor and line state scale combinations?
